selfCorrection.summary: ADV-D056-01 is a MUST-FIX I did not raise, and it identifies a defect of a kind my earlier misses did not cover. I consented to turn 1 at 0/0.
selfCorrection.whatTurn1Said: Turn 1 called itself a 'RULE-GOVERNED register-content evaluation rule', declared 'Does not amend D-001's five conditions', and described its own effect as stating 'how SATISFIED is evidenced' for a narrow class. Its clause 1 reinterpreted file 08's SATISFIED legend 'for those eligible rows'.
selfCorrection.whyThatIsAMustFix: Reinterpreting the legend for a class of rows overrides live governing text. D-015 records that DR-102 'stays OPEN, because the classes are specifications and no harness executes them', and the live DR-102 cell says the row 'remains slice-affecting and open until the hostile-conformance classes are executed by a harness at DR-G21 via ID-DEP-3'. Turn 1 would have authorised a later SATISFIED that those two sentences forbid, while asserting nothing was amended. That is a successor amendment, and an unnamed one leaves two live conflicting SATISFIED rules with no statement of which governs or how to restore the old one.
selfCorrection.howIMissedIt: I verified what the instrument does and never asked what it displaces. My turn-1 verdict tested the grant, the narrowness, the thirty-row partition, the Class B scope, and whether the execution gate was removed or relocated — all sound. It did not ask which existing authorities the rule overrides. The aggravating detail is that I quoted the DR-102 cell's execution requirement in that verdict myself, as a premise establishing that the deadlock was real. I used the live bar as evidence for the argument and never turned round to ask what the rule did to the bar.
selfCorrection.howThisDiffersFromMyEarlierMisses: The earlier ones were a citation resolving to the wrong referent, stale values in text I had not read, and an unread grant field. This is none of those: every fact I checked was right. The failure was in the question set. I treated 'Does not amend D-001's five conditions' as a refusal to credit rather than as a claim to test — the test being 'then what does it amend?'
selfCorrection.correctiveDiscipline: When an instrument changes how an existing rule is applied, enumerate the live authorities its operation displaces and check that the entry names each one, states its post-change status, and can restore it on overturn. A 'Does not amend X' line narrows the claim to X; it is not evidence that nothing else is amended. Turn 2's three-part structure — What is superseded and what stands, the MF-6 removal in Eligibility (5), and a reversibility clause naming what reverts — is the template I should have looked for and did not.

summary: Subject, prompt and the frozen turn-1 subject all held. The repair is substantial and honest: the entry now calls itself a scoped successor amendment in its decision type, adds a 'What is superseded, and what stands' section, and extends reversibility to restore the pre-amendment state. I verified both sentences it claims to supersede against their sources — D-015's clause and the live DR-102 cell — and both exist and say what the entry says. It also closes the two-authorities problem that an unnamed amendment would have created: Eligibility (5) now requires the MF-6 edit to remove the cell's conflicting bar, so the old and new rules never govern the same row at once. The substance from turn 1 is intact: all thirty condition-2 rows still accounted for, the same four eligible in kind, DR-103, DR-105 and DR-118 still ineligible, no row marked SATISFIED, no token coined, condition 2 still NOT MET.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: dfb0c2af39ff31df9bf3609c131f03ee2d87a585dcd684abd633d47ffb11ed82, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value. Prompt held at e9fe241a… across start and end. The turn-1 subject re-measures at d4b628f6…, matching the pinned value.

The attack 'ADV-D056-01 not landed' fails. The decision type now reads 'RULE-GOVERNED. Scoped successor amendment to SATISFIED *evidence* for a named eligible class, and to D-015's SATISFIED-rejection for that class.' The header's refusal narrowed from 'Does not amend D-001's five conditions' to 'Does not rewrite D-001's five checklist bullets', which is the accurate claim. Clause 3 now reads 'This entry changes how SATISFIED is evidenced for the eligible class' where turn 1 read 'states how'. And the alternatives add 'Claim this is only an evaluation rule and leave D-015's SATISFIED-rejection live. Rejected: ADV-D056-01.'

Both superseded sentences exist and are accurately characterised — the check that matters most, since an amendment that supersedes text which does not exist, or mis-states it, is worse than one that supersedes nothing. D-015 reads 'the row stays `OPEN`, because the classes are specifications and no harness executes them', which the entry quotes as 'stays OPEN because the classes are specifications and no harness executes them'. The live DR-102 cell reads '…it remains slice-affecting and open until the hostile-conformance classes are executed by a harness at DR-G21 via ID-DEP-3', which the entry characterises as the cell's 'not SATISFIED until the hostile-conformance classes are executed'. Both are faithful.

The supersession is bounded three ways: to the eligible class only, to those sentences' effect as a SATISFIED bar rather than as description — 'Those sentences remain history and remain true as a description of qualification. They are no longer the governing SATISFIED rule for an eligible row' — and to rows meeting the five-gate Eligibility test.

The two-authorities problem is closed rather than left open. Eligibility (5) now requires the MF-6 edit to record SATISFIED 'and removes the cell's conflicting "until executed" / "until measured" SATISFIED-bar'. Clause 2 states 'Two authorities will not remain in conflict at the moment of that re-record: the re-record's MF-6 edit is what removes the cell-level bar.' Clause 4 adds that today's cells 'are not a second live SATISFIED rule for an eligible row once that later edit lands.' So the old bar is removed by the same act that relies on the new rule.

Reversibility now restores the pre-amendment state explicitly, which an unnamed amendment could not have done: 'Overturn restores D-015's SATISFIED-rejection as the governing SATISFIED rule for DR-102, restores the live-cell "until executed" / "until measured" bars as governing, and restores the pre-amendment reading of the SATISFIED legend.' Three restorations for three displacements.

The 'Stands' list is accurate against sources. D-015 does record control-protocol-contract.v2 as DR-102's accepted design contract; D-013 does record component-manifest-schemas.v2 for DR-103, and its alternative (a) rejection — 'SATISFIED is legend-defined as "exact acceptance evidence is linked and independently reviewed", and the fourth element is unmet' — is the SATISFIED-refusal the entry says stands for DR-103 until fixture authoring exists; D-006, D-008 and D-009 are the Class B decisions; and D-001's five checklist bullets are untouched.

The turn-1 substance survives unchanged where it should. Expanding the shorthand again, all thirty condition-2 rows remain accounted for with none unaccounted; the eligible-in-kind set is still exactly DR-102, DR-115, DR-119 and DR-123; and DR-103, DR-105 and DR-118 remain in the ineligible table, with DR-103's entry strengthened by 'D-013's SATISFIED-refusal stands until that authoring exists.'

The attacks 'this entry marks DR-102 / DR-103 / DR-115 SATISFIED', 'rewrites D-001's five checklist bullets', 'coins DESIGN-ACCEPTED', 'treats harness naming as SATISFIED', 'treats execution as architecture SATISFIED', 'extends D-070's union to condition 2', 'silent deferral', 'Class B silently SATISFIES', 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' and 'file 08 edited' all fail on clauses carried from turn 1 and re-counted here, including 'This entry marks no row SATISFIED', 'No SATISFIED re-record', 'Coordinator fiat remains unlawful (DR-204)', 'condition 2 remains NOT MET' and 'Zero SATISFIED is added'. file 08 measures at its cited digest and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture.

The attack 'D-015 design-contract recording overturned' fails: it is the first item under 'Stands', the readiness effect repeats 'D-015's design-contract recording stands', and only the SATISFIED-rejection is superseded, for the eligible class only.

A new rejected alternative closes the obvious cheaper route and explains why it is worse: 'Use a condition-2 deferral of the execution remainder instead of amending SATISFIED evidence. Rejected for slice-affecting rows whose design contract is already the architecture outcome (DR-102 / D-015). Deferral would pretend the protocol surface is out of the preview. The honest successor is this SATISFIED-evidence amendment.'

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The repair is the right one and it is candid: turn 2 says outright that turn 1 'tried to resolve that deadlock while saying D-001 and the live cells were unamended' and that the other reviewer was right. It then does the three things an amendment has to do — names what it supersedes and what stands, ensures the old and new rules never govern the same row simultaneously by making the MF-6 re-record remove the cell bar, and states what an overturn restores. I verified both superseded sentences against their sources rather than accepting the entry's account of them. My self-correction is recorded in full: I consented to turn 1 having checked what the instrument does and never having asked what it displaces, and I quoted the very sentence it displaces in that verdict as a premise of the argument. A 'does not amend X' line is a claim to test, not a refusal to credit.
